item.text: {"text":"HSTU already incorporates learned relative-position and bucketed elapsed-time biases inside SiLU attention; temporal conditioning is native to the family ([original paper, 2024](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v235/main/assets/zhai24a/zhai24a.pdf)). The clearest controlled evidence comes from [Scaling New Frontiers](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=e6pqwHR1Yh): on MovieLens-20M, HR@10 was 0.3376 with position+time, 0.3356 with time alone, 0.3122 with position alone, and 0.3083 without attention bias. Time supplied most of the observed benefit; position added a smaller increment. These results support testing elapsed-time conditioning, but do not establish persistent/transient interest separation or transfer to the four Amazon categories.\n\nAdjacent evidence argues against assuming monotonically stronger recency. [Long-Term Interest Clock, WWW 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15817) retrieves older behaviors relevant to the current time and candidate, then aggregates them with time-gap-aware attention, supporting recurring temporal relevance. This is a different architecture and task, not an HSTU ablation. Research implication: within one jointly trained HSTU per category, compare position-only, time-only, and combined biases under identical training; add timestamp-shuffling controls and inspect performance by elapsed-gap strata. Use unconstrained learned temporal buckets rather than imposing decay. Deletion sensitivity alone cannot identify intent drift; any interpretation of persistent/transient interests remains a hypothesis requiring additional controlled evidence."}
